output.title: Deadline for a Prescriber to Schedule a Peer-to-Peer Review After a Pharmacy Denial
output.draft_text:
Question: How many days does a prescriber have to schedule a peer-to-peer review after a denial?

Answer: After a prior authorization or coverage request is denied, the prescriber has [number of days] [calendar/business] days from [the date of the denial notice / the date the denial was issued / the date the prescriber received the denial] to request a peer-to-peer review.

How the prescriber schedules it: The prescriber or their office should contact [department or team name] at [phone number / fax number / portal or other request method]. Peer-to-peer reviews are available [hours and days of availability, including time zone]. When requesting, the prescriber should have [required information, e.g., member ID, denial or case reference number, drug name].

Who conducts the review: The review is conducted between the prescriber and [title of reviewer, e.g., clinical pharmacist or medical director].

If the deadline has passed: If the prescriber does not request a peer-to-peer review within [number of days] days, [what happens next, e.g., the prescriber or member may file a formal appeal, and any applicable appeal deadline of [number of days] days].

Does a peer-to-peer affect appeal rights? Requesting a peer-to-peer review [does / does not] pause or extend the deadline to file a formal appeal. [Confirm relationship between peer-to-peer and appeal timelines.]

Exceptions: [Any plan types, lines of business, drug categories, or urgent/expedited situations where a different peer-to-peer timeframe applies, or where peer-to-peer is not offered.]

Advocate tip: Encourage the prescriber's office to act promptly and to note the denial date shown on the denial letter so they can track the [number of days]-day window.

author_checklist: Confirm the exact number of days a prescriber has to request or schedule a peer-to-peer review after a denial.
Confirm whether the timeframe is counted in calendar days or business days.
Confirm the event that starts the clock (denial issue date, notice date, or date received).
Confirm whether the deadline is to request the peer-to-peer or to complete it.
Confirm the correct contact method, department, phone/fax numbers, and portal details for scheduling.
Confirm hours of availability and time zone for peer-to-peer reviews.
Confirm what information the prescriber must provide when requesting.
Confirm who conducts the review on the plan side.
Confirm what options remain if the peer-to-peer window is missed, including formal appeal deadlines.
Confirm whether requesting a peer-to-peer pauses or extends the formal appeal deadline.
Confirm whether timeframes differ by line of business (e.g., commercial, Medicare, Medicaid), state regulation, client contract, or expedited/urgent requests.
Confirm whether any drug categories or denial types are excluded from peer-to-peer review.
Cite the source policy or contract document supporting each confirmed fact.
Remove any placeholders or sections that do not apply before approval.
